title: NYC Daily Digest
text:
☀️ Good morning, Matthew! It's Wednesday, November 11, 2026, Veterans Day.

🌤️ Weather
Mostly sunny and mild for November. It's a cool start, then a high of about 62–65°F and a low tonight in the low 50s. Rain chance is close to 0% today, with clouds moving in tonight and possibly a late shower. Tomorrow looks wet (about 90% chance of rain).
What to wear: a light jacket or sweater is enough today. Keep an umbrella handy for tomorrow.

🗞️ Headlines
• House Republicans narrowly blocked Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. Trump had urged Congress to "stand up for Pete."
• Iran: Trump met with a key Qatari mediator about ending the war and said new strikes are "highly unlikely" if talks progress. A Reuters/Ipsos poll says 71% of Americans want Congress to act to end the war.
• Lame duck on the Hill: Trump is pushing the Senate to pass permitting reform and confirm 161 judicial nominees before Democrats take over both chambers in January.
• NYC: Mayor Mamdani signed the COPA law, which gives nonprofits first chance to buy about 2,100 distressed residential buildings citywide.
• NYC: A federal judge ordered the city to comply with an ICE subpoena for records on residents of a Bronx shelter. City Hall says it is "evaluating next steps."

🚇 Getting around
• A train: no service between Rockaway Blvd and Ozone Park–Lefferts Blvd through 5 a.m. Monday, Nov 16, because of signal work. Lefferts-bound trains run to Howard Beach–JFK instead.
• 1 train: the southbound bypass in Harlem continues (through Dec 18).
• Expect street closures along Fifth Avenue in the 20s–40s for the parade.
• Check the MTA app before you head out.

🎉 NYC today
• The 107th NYC Veterans Day Parade, the nation's largest, runs up Fifth Avenue from about 26th St to 45th St, roughly 12:30 to 3:30 p.m., rain or shine. A wreath-laying in Madison Square Park comes first, around 11 a.m.
• It's a great afternoon for a walk. Enjoy the sun before Thursday's rain.

💡 Nugget
On Veterans Day, alternate-side parking is suspended, but parking meters stay in effect. Post offices and banks are closed, and the subway runs on a normal schedule.
